column1: # p332 — 2026-10-20. The H5P ORG GRANT CENSUS across THREE channels, every cell first-hand.
# WHY it was run: the delivery audit put `h5p/h5p-interactive-video` at the top of its defect
# class — permissive, deferred, 15 sightings since p195 (2026-10-14), never on a shelf. The
# cause turned out to be the CHANNEL, not the write: its grant does not exist as a file.
# Channels, in the order this KB's grant ladder tries them:
#   1 FILE     raw.githubusercontent.com/<slug>/HEAD/{LICENSE,LICENSE.txt,LICENSE.md,COPYING}
#   2 MANIFEST package.json / composer.json "license" key
#   3 README   the licence text carried in the README body
# 🔴 THE RESULT: 8 of 10 repositories have NO LICENCE FILE. Seven of the eight grants found are
# invisible to channel 1. A ladder that leads with the file channel and does not fall through
# reads this org as almost entirely ungranted. It is not.

column1: # 🟢 THE SPLIT IS REAL AND IT FOLLOWS THE RENDERER/CONTENT BOUNDARY: the PHP core that renders
# H5P is GPL-3.0; the content types are MIT. This is STRICTLY MORE than this KB's shelves have
# recorded. verticals/solutions.md has said a studio may author "H5P content JSON with an agent;
# the renderer stays untouched, so GPL stays contained" — true, and it understates the surface.
# A studio may FORK AND MODIFY A CONTENT TYPE under MIT, which is a code surface, not a data one.
# 🟡 Caveat to carry to a client: the grant is PER REPOSITORY and the org is not uniform. Three
# content types state MIT only in the README body, and `h5p-core` states nothing anywhere. Read
# the specific content type you intend to fork; do not generalise from the four clean rows.
